You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image retain photographic subject matter and appearance?
node.criteria: Pass if the subject matter remains recognizably photographic; fail if photographic subject matter or appearance is not retained; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
node.binding: Assess the supplied image as edited for photographic subject matter and appearance alongside any stylistic changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image retains recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance: the street scene, vehicles, buildings, and traffic signal remain depicted with photographic detail, despite some stylization.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria correctly distinguish the two required aspects, and the traces support photographic appearance while finding no clear comic-book treatment. The mismatch is therefore not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: both checks ran validly, and the edited image remains visibly photographic with no evident illustrated outlines, halftone, or comparable comic styling. Do not relabel this as absent solely to match the reference; the rubric defines partial when any requested component is present, and retained photographic appearance is evidence of one component. Instead, investigate whether s2 is bound too broadly: it may be counting unchanged source content as edit progress, although the instruction asks for a comic-book photo and the rubric says unrelated edits do not count. Clarify whether fulfillment measures the requested final appearance or progress attributable to the edit, and ensure the photographic criterion requires the requested photographic quality rather than mere retention of recognizable scene content. Preserve the separate comic-styling check and the partial/unknown rules; do not weaken either requirement to force agreement.

Keep this criterion distinct from the separate comic-styling check, and do not treat photographic retention alone as evidence that the requested edit progressed. In these images, the edited scene remains photographic and appears largely similar to the source; that supports retention, but does not establish comic-book treatment or attributable progress. Preserve the rubric’s partial/unknown rules and avoid forcing the reference label. The trace is valid and dependency-free, so this is a criterion/binding issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
